chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who prays two rak'ahs, then remembers in the second while bowing that he missed a prostration in the first. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you miss a prostration in the first rak'ah and do not know whether it is one or two, face forward until two are valid for you. And if it is in the third and fourth, and you miss a prostration after you have maintained the bowing, you must repeat the prostration.'
And this report does not contradict [other reports].
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I realize I missed a prostration during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific mechanics of *sujood al-sahw* (prostration of forgetfulness) when a worshipper is uncertain about the number of prostrations missed in the first rak'ah. It establishes that if the doubt occurs in the first rak'ah, one must face forward to ensure two complete prostrations are validated, whereas missing a prostration in later rak'ahs after having secured the ruku' requires simply repeating the missed sujood. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual validity while accommodating human error through specific corrective actions.
